# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
All recommendations in FDA-DOSE-OPT-2024 shall be implemented without deviation, and any investigator request to adapt them requires prior FDA approval.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
After identifying the first tolerable dose, all subsequent participants will receive only that dose, with no concurrent or sequential comparison of alternative dose levels.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The study will select the recommended Phase 2 dose from the first expansion cohort without collecting dose–response data or evaluating effects of long-term administration, concomitant medications, or comorbid disease.
The formulation-bridging expansion cohort will enroll participants receiving the new tablet or legacy capsule, with safety and pharmacokinetic results summarized descriptively and no prespecified comparison objectives or analysis methods.
For this intravenous oncology study, the 500 mg dose will be prepared as a 50 mg/mL solution, requiring administration of 10 mL over 5 minutes regardless of infusion-site tolerance or participant body size.
The disease-specific expansion cohort will enroll up to 60 participants without interim futility monitoring or prespecified criteria for discontinuing enrollment for inadequate response.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN))이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_012.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

ev_013.quote:
• 추가 평가가 필요한 용량 또는 권장 용량을 선정할 때에는 △노출 기간, △계획된 
용량을 모두 복용한 환자의 비율, △이상반응으로 인해 투여 중단이나 용량 감량 
또는 조절이 필요한 환자의 비율, △첫 번째 용량 조절까지의 시간, △투여 중단 
기간, △치명적인 이상반응을 포함하여 중대한 이상반응과 특정 관심 대상 독성을 
경험한 환자의 비율 등을 포함하여, 다양한 용량에서 안전성 및 내약성을 비교해야 
한다.
• 과도한 독성에 대한 중단 기준은 사전에 명시해야 한다. 허용하는 독성의 종류 및 
비율은 개발 단계, 약물의 특성, 질병 단계 등 다양한 요인에 의해 달라질 수 있다.
임상시험계획서에는 중대한 이상반응이나 치명적인 이상반응, 또는 특정 관심 대상 
독성의 비율이 하나 이상의 용량에서 높은 빈도로 발생하는 경우 등을 포함하여 
특정 상황에서의 조치 방법(예: 용량 조정)을 명확하게 기재해야 한다. 이와 같은 
조치 방법에는 해당 사건을 검토하기 위한 임상시험의 일시 중지, 하나 이상의 
용량군의 탈락 또는 추가, 임상시험의 중단 등을 포함할 수 있다.
• 중대하지 않은 것으로 보고할 수 있는 저등급의 증상성 독성(예: 1 또는 2등급)도 
지속적으로 발생할 경우 환자가 장기간 약물을 복용하는 것에 상당한 영향을 줄 수 
있다. 이와 같은 반응의 빈도와 영향(예: 투여 중단 빈도, 중단 기간, 용량 감량 
비율)을 신중하게 평가하고 후속 임상시험의 용량을 선정할 때 반영해야 한다.
• 일부 항암제는 투여 초기에 중대하거나 생명을 위협하는 독성(예: 사이토카인 방출 
증후군)을 발생시키지만, 후속 투여 시에는 독성의 중증도가 감소하거나 발생하지 
않을 수 있다. 내약성을 개선하기 위해서 용량 적정과 같은 투여 전략을 평가하는 
것을 고려할 수 있다.
• 환자-보고 결과(Patient-reported outcome, PRO)는 예상하는 증상성 부작용과 환자 
기능에 미치는 영향을 체계적이고 정량적으로 평가할 수 있다. 용량 결정 시험 및

ev_014.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_014.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

ev_015.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_015.quote:
Risk control should be proportionate to the importance of the risk to participant s’ 
rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of trial results. Risk mitigation 
activities may be incorporated, for example, in protocol design and implementation, 
monitoring plans, agreements between parties defining roles and responsibilities, and 
training.  
Where relevant, the sponsor should set pre-specified acceptable ranges (e.g., quality 
tolerance limits at the tr ial level) to support the control of risks 
to critical to quality factors. These pre -specified ranges reflect limits that when 
exceeded have the potential to impact participant safety or the reliability of trial 
results. Where deviation beyond these ranges is detected , an evaluation should be 
performed to determine if there is a possible systemic issue and if action is needed.

항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인
 1. 서론
 항암제 초기 임상시험의 주된 목적 중 하나는 다음 단계의 임상시험에서 추가 평가가 
필요한 용량을 결정하는 것이다. 항암제는 약물의 작용기전과 투여받는 환자 집단의 
특수성으로 인해 암 치료 효과를 극대화하면서 부작용은 최소화 할 수 있는 적절한 
수준의 용량이 요구된다. 과도한 용량은 심각한 부작용을 유발할 수 있으며, 반대로 
부족한 용량은 암세포의 효과적인 제거가 어려워 결국 치료의 실패로 이어질 수 있다.
 본 가이드라인은 항암제 중 저분자(small molecule) 의약품의 임상시험에서 최적의 
용량을 파악하기 위한 전략을 구체적으로 안내함으로써 개발 및 제품화에 도움을 
주고자 마련하였다. 방사성 의약품, 세포 및 유전자 치료제, 암 치료 목적의 백신 및 
생약 성분의 항암제 등은 별도의 논의가 필요하며, 인체 최초 임상시험(First-in-human,
FIH)에서 시작 용량의 선택에 대한 내용은 포함하지 않는다.
2. 배경
 일반적으로 항암제의 권장 2상 용량(Recommended phase 2 dose, RP2D)을 결정하기 
위한 용량 탐색 시험은 용량 증량 및 용량 확장을 포함하며 최대 내약 용량(Maximal
tolerated dose, MTD)을 결정할 수 있도록 설계한다. 이는 세포독성 화학요법의 
용량-반응 곡선이 가파르고 약물 표적에 대한 특이성이 제한적이나, 심각하고 생명을 
위협하는 암 질환에 대한 효과적인 대안이 부족함으로 인해 상당한 독성은 감수할 
필요가 있음을 고려한 방법이다. MTD는 소수의 시험대상자에서 용량을 단계적으로 
증량하면서 짧은 기간 동안 중증 또는 생명을 위협하는 용량 제한 독성(Dose limiting
toxicity, DLT)이 사전에 지정된 비율까지 도달하는지 여부를 평가하여 결정한다. 또한 
일반적으로 후속 임상시험에서는 MTD 또는 MTD에 가까운 용량을 선정한다.
 키나제 억제제와 같이 최근 개발하는 항암제는 대부분 종양에 중요한 분자적 경로와 
상호 작용하도록 설계한다(즉 표적 치료제). 이와 같은 약물은 세포독성 화학요법 대비 
더 넓은 치료 지수를 가지면서 다른 용량-반응 관계를 나타내는 경우가 많기 때문에

review_questions.hypothesis: DV-101’s SMILES contains an acrylamide electrophilic warhead consistent with covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors; identity and potency should be confirmed from authoritative chemical and bioactivity records without inferring organ toxicity from structure.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Confirm exact structure/identity against sotorasib records and retrieve KRAS G12C biochemical and cellular potency distributions from ChEMBL or primary sources; refute if the structure maps to another compound or lacks the expected covalent warhead.
review_questions.protocol_span: DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.
review_questions.search_query: sotorasib ChEMBL SMILES KRAS G12C IC50 covalent acrylamide

review_questions.hypothesis: The liver-test schedule may match the baseline sotorasib label but may not address enhanced monitoring warranted after recent anti-PD-(L)1 therapy or abnormal results.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare the current FDA label’s hepatotoxicity warning, routine and intensified monitoring intervals, and evidence concerning recent immunotherapy. Confirm whether Appendix B triggers more frequent tests and specifies withholding, reduction, or discontinuation.
review_questions.protocol_span: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.

review_questions.hypothesis: Dose-modification adequacy cannot be established because the operative hepatotoxicity and ILD/pneumonitis rules are absent from the supplied protocol text.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect Appendix B for grade-specific interruption, resumption, dose-reduction, permanent-discontinuation, and recurrent-toxicity rules; compare them with the current sotorasib label, including immediate withholding for suspected ILD/pneumonitis.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
review_questions.search_query: FDA sotorasib prescribing information dosage modifications hepatotoxicity ILD pneumonitis

review_questions.hypothesis: The protocol does not prespecify an exposure–response analysis linking individual exposure to efficacy and toxicity, so dose proportionality and trough summaries alone may not support RP2D selection.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review Appendix D and the statistical analysis plan for exposure–efficacy and exposure–toxicity models, covariates, estimands, uncertainty, and handling of dose modifications; compare expected exposure overlap with labeled sotorasib PK.
review_questions.protocol_span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

review_questions.hypothesis: Trough-only PK in randomized cohorts may be inadequate to compare AUC and Cmax across candidate doses or characterize exposure changes from time-varying adherence, interactions, or dose modification.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Determine whether population-PK modeling, timed post-dose samples, dosing records, bioanalytical validation, and covariate collection can reliably estimate individual AUC/Cmax and steady-state exposure in both randomized arms.
review_questions.protocol_span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts.
review_questions.search_query: FDA population pharmacokinetics guidance sparse sampling exposure response dose optimization

review_questions.hypothesis: BOIN adequacy is unverifiable without cohort rules, dose-skipping constraints, DLT window, evaluability rules, stopping boundaries, and scenario-specific simulation results.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect Appendix C and the full design for escalation/de-escalation boundaries, cohort size, overdose control, replacement rules, early stopping, dose-selection method, and simulation metrics across clinically plausible toxicity curves with 36 subjects.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose finding trial design simulation operating characteristics BOIN Project Optimus

review_questions.hypothesis: The instruction to treat only the first tolerable dose contradicts the later randomized two-dose comparison and would prevent comparative dose optimization if operationally applied.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Reconcile which provision controls enrollment. Confirm that escalation can nominate at least two suitable doses and that randomized comparison occurs before RP2D selection rather than assigning all later participants to one dose.
review_questions.protocol_span: After identifying the first tolerable dose, all subsequent participants will receive only that dose, with no concurrent or sequential comparison of alternative dose levels.
review_questions.search_query: FDA Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for Oncology Diseases randomized parallel dose comparison guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: Selecting RP2D from the first expansion cohort without dose–response or longer-term tolerability evidence conflicts with integrated dosage optimization principles and contradicts the stated randomized comparison.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Determine whether this sentence is operative. Verify comparative dose–response, cumulative toxicity, dose intensity, concomitant-medication, and comorbidity data are incorporated into Appendix D before RP2D selection.
review_questions.protocol_span: The study will select the recommended Phase 2 dose from the first expansion cohort without collecting dose–response data or evaluating effects of long-term administration, concomitant medications, or comorbid disease.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dosage optimization long-term tolerability dose response concomitant medications comorbidities guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The formulation-bridging cohort lacks prespecified comparison objectives and methods, so descriptive summaries may not establish comparable exposure or safety between tablet and capsule formulations.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Look for predefined PK comparability metrics, exposure parameters, confidence intervals, sample-size rationale, food and dosing controls, safety estimands, and decision criteria governing whether formulations can be pooled or bridged.
review_questions.protocol_span: The formulation-bridging expansion cohort will enroll participants receiving the new tablet or legacy capsule, with safety and pharmacokinetic results summarized descriptively and no prespecified comparison objectives or analysis methods.
review_questions.search_query: FDA bioavailability bioequivalence studies orally administered drug products formulation bridging PK guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The intravenous 500 mg instruction is incompatible with the orally administered sotorasib study and introduces an apparent wrong-route, wrong-dose medication hazard.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Confirm the sentence is erroneous and remove it from all protocol, pharmacy, and site-facing documents. Verify formulation, route, strengths, preparation, administration, and accountability consistently specify oral DV-101.
review_questions.protocol_span: For this intravenous oncology study, the 500 mg dose will be prepared as a 50 mg/mL solution, requiring administration of 10 mL over 5 minutes regardless of infusion-site tolerance or participant body size.
review_questions.search_query: ICH E6 protocol investigational product dose route administration medication error consistency

review_questions.hypothesis: Enrolling up to 60 disease-specific expansion participants without futility monitoring or stopping criteria may expose participants and consume sample size despite inadequate activity or unacceptable toxicity.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Verify a cohort-specific statistical rationale, response assumptions, precision or power, interim timing, futility and toxicity boundaries, enrollment suspension rules, and multiplicity handling where multiple tumor cohorts are contemplated.
review_questions.protocol_span: The disease-specific expansion cohort will enroll up to 60 participants without interim futility monitoring or prespecified criteria for discontinuing enrollment for inadequate response.
review_questions.search_query: FDA expansion cohorts first in human oncology trials cohort size stopping rules futility guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The four-week anti-PD-(L)1 washout may not adequately control delayed immune toxicity or sotorasib-associated hepatotoxicity risk in recently exposed participants.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare approved-label evidence, published sotorasib trials, and analogous KRAS G12C protocols for washout duration, baseline recovery, steroid restrictions, liver-test eligibility, and enhanced monitoring stratified by time since checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

review_questions.hypothesis: The statement that every recommendation must be implemented without deviation mischaracterizes FDA guidance as binding and incorrectly implies investigator adaptations require prior FDA approval.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve the final guidance’s nonbinding-language clause and applicable IND protocol-amendment requirements. Distinguish sponsor protocol control, IRB review, immediately necessary hazard changes, and changes requiring FDA submission rather than prior approval.
review_questions.protocol_span: All recommendations in FDA-DOSE-OPT-2024 shall be implemented without deviation, and any investigator request to adapt them requires prior FDA approval.

review_questions.what_to_verify: Identify whether relevant MFDS materials are statutes, regulations, notices, or civil guidance; verify Korean requirements for protocol changes, scientific dose rationale, expansion sample size, stopping rules, and MFDS/IRB reporting or approval.
